notes: V1 has been reset to the shared_backbone_fpn_coarse_to_fine_local_moe architecture. round_018 showed that directly inserting randomly initialized ROI adapter layers into a warm-started student is invalid and causes catastrophic regression. round_019 replaced that path with a residual zero-init ROI adapter and became the old-definition best saved holdout checkpoint. On 2026-03-25 the strict-corner metric line was migrated: point_le_0_01_ratio now means per-corner <0.01 hit ratio, and max_corner_le_0_03_ratio was added as the page-level strict corner metric. round_022 switched sampling to max_corner_error hard examples and checkpoint selection to max_corner_le_0_03_ratio, reaching the local max-corner best at point_error_mean 0.0213, point_le_0_01_ratio 0.0905, and max_corner_le_0_03_ratio 0.2039. round_025 added an explicit max-corner supervision term; its saved checkpoint reached point_le_0_01_ratio 0.1217, but the real intra-round peak was epoch_002 at 0.1250. round_026 recovered max-corner behavior with quad inset regularization but lost strict-point gain. round_027 proved that demoting point_le_0_01_ratio to an observation-only metric did not restore student quality. round_028 restored point_le_0_01_ratio as the checkpoint metric, enforced avg_page_infer_ms <= 500 as a hard gate, and added strict-point-oriented sampling plus loss, but the holdout result still fell back to 0.0839. round_029 to round_031 then explored scene-aware MoE routing with automatic scene recognition on top of the coarse-to-fine student. round_029 surfaced a router/expert warm-start incompatibility. round_030 fixed the scene-input path but still missed hidden-width compatibility and collapsed further. round_031 finally restored full router/expert warm-start compatibility via zero-init residual scene adaptation and recovered to point_le_0_01_ratio 0.0872 at 9.63 ms, but still did not beat round_029=0.0905 or the round_025 peak. round_032 then added explicit process distillation for ROI-stage geometry plus corner-structure visibility, edge direction, and fallback cues. That heavier process branch kept latency within budget but the saved checkpoint dropped to point_le_0_01_ratio 0.0773, which means full structure-cue supervision over-regularized the student. round_033 reduced process supervision to mostly geometry-only distillation and recovered the saved checkpoint to 0.0938 at 11.93 ms. round_034 and round_035 confirmed that geometry-process continuation and ROI-stage-only supervision both plateau below round_033. round_036 returned to the historical strict-point line by hot-starting from round_025 epoch_002 and mixing max-corner plus light strict-point supervision, but still only reached 0.0888 at 9.48 ms. round_037 then ran the cleanest control: near-round_025 recipe, epoch_002 hot-start, lower augmentation, and strict-point checkpoint selection. It recovered to 0.1102 at 9.04 ms, which is the best post-round_025 continuation so far, but still failed to match the original 0.1250 peak. round_038 tried to preserve the same line with even softer augmentation; it fell to 0.0954 at 9.09 ms. round_039 then performed a one-epoch low-augmentation continuation from round_037 itself; it also stayed at 0.0954, although latency improved to 7.55 ms. round_040 finally switched to explicit strict-point hard-example plus scene-balanced resampling; it reached only 0.0987 at 8.97 ms. round_041 followed with a one-epoch low-augmentation replay from round_040 and dropped to 0.0806 at 9.24 ms. On 2026-03-26 the line moved to a new strict-point split_v2 with 397/60/134 manual train/val/holdout pages. round_042 established the new split_v2 baseline at 0.0896 point_le_0_01_ratio and 8.91 ms, but its epoch history showed the true strict-point peak appeared at epoch_001 rather than the selected epoch_003. round_043 then replayed from round_042 epoch_001 with lower augmentation and lifted split_v2 holdout point_le_0_01_ratio to 0.1455 at 9.58 ms, but with severe inward shrink and broad geometry regression. round_044 to round_050 showed that anti-inset tuning and residual or blend-residual heads improve geometry and wider-threshold metrics, but not the primary strict-point metric. round_051 and round_052 showed that both full-ROI strict spatial decoding and per-corner patch residual strict-heads fail on the current unified student. round_053 showed that ranking only the student's own coarse, roi_stage, and base_final outputs improves geometry but still leaves point_le_0_01_ratio at 0.0728. round_054 extended the pool with OpenCV best candidates and improved geometry further, but strict-point regressed again to 0.0653. round_055 froze the entire student except candidate_selection_head and trained only the selector; that recovered strict-point only to 0.0765 while lowering latency to 6.8 ms. The decisive finding was that the hidden coarse candidate itself was already strong: re-evaluation of round_053 and round_054 showed coarse_quad alone reaching about 0.7034 to 0.7052 point_le_0_01_ratio on split_v2 holdout. round_056 then formalized that insight by switching the final output strategy to coarse-preserving and training only the coarse heads. round_057 then reopened the shared backbone together with the coarse heads at very low learning rate, improving only geometry but not the primary metric. Before round_058, an offline analysis showed base_final still lost to coarse on 131/134 holdout pages for point_error and 124/134 pages for max_corner_error, which ruled out simple selective-refine gating. round_058 then removed the conflicting v28-driven final supervision from the coarse-preserving line and tightened training to manual + r3 dominated coarse distillation. That lifted split_v2 holdout point_le_0_01_ratio from 0.7127 to 0.7164 while keeping latency at 6.62 ms. round_059 kept the corrected loss and reopened the shared backbone/FPN at low learning rate. It held point_le_0_01_ratio at 0.7164, improved max_corner_le_0_03_ratio to 0.7836, but did not move the primary metric further. round_060 tested a materially different coarse line by increasing input/output resolution from 256/64 to 320/80. That clearly regressed split_v2 holdout to point_le_0_01_ratio 0.6754 and 9.08 ms, so the current bottleneck is not simply input resolution. round_061 then returned to 256/64, kept the corrected coarse-preserving output, and increased r3-distillation strength while freezing training back down to the coarse heads. It recovered to the round_058 strict-point level at 0.7164, improved max_corner_le_0_03_ratio to 0.7761, and reduced latency to 6.56 ms. round_062 added reliability-gated r3 distillation in code: r3 heatmap and quad supervision only apply when r3 and manual quad agree within a configured threshold. That change is covered by tests, but the first gated experiment still held at 0.7164 and 6.61 ms, so the plateau is not explained by simple tail-noise filtering either. round_063 then introduced a per-corner adaptive manual/r3 blended coarse target together with r3-based hard-example sampling, but the best holdout point_le_0_01_ratio fell to 0.7090 at 6.49 ms. round_064 isolated the curriculum change by returning to the round_061 corrected coarse loss and keeping only r3-based sampling; it still stayed at 0.7090, although latency dropped to 5.72 ms. round_065 then introduced a high-confidence coarse curriculum by filtering train pages to stronger r3 examples before warmup; by itself that only recovered to 0.7127. round_066 brought that warmup checkpoint back to the full train set and restored the old 0.7164 platform with better max_corner geometry but no primary-metric gain. round_067 finally combined the curriculum line with low-learning-rate reopening of the shared backbone/FPN and coarse heads; that broke the old platform and lifted split_v2 holdout point_le_0_01_ratio to 0.7239. round_068 then froze back down to the coarse heads and preserved the same 0.7239 strict-point level while reducing average inference to 6.45 ms, making it the current best saved split_v2 checkpoint under the user's metric order. round_069 performed a final ultra-short replay from round_068 and regressed strict-point to 0.6978 despite better wide-threshold geometry, which indicates round_068 is the local peak of this new curriculum line. round_070 then tested weak-scene-targeted sampling on low_contrast_scene and near_color_background; it improved point_error_mean and max_corner geometry but still regressed the primary strict-point metric to 0.7071. round_071 then tested a narrower reopening shape from round_068 by opening only stage3, lat2, lat3, and the coarse heads; it matched 0.7239 but could not exceed it and slightly worsened latency. round_072 then tested a high-confidence r3 exactness polish by training only the coarse heads on r3-perfect train pages; validation improved but holdout regressed sharply to 0.7127, which means easy-page rehearsal hurts generalization. round_073 then switched the adaptive coarse target to an r3-priority per-corner teacher switch; it approached the current best but still stopped at 0.7201. round_074 then added a new oracle coarse teacher target in code that picks the lower-error corner between r3 and v28 for each supervised corner; targeted and full regression tests cover this behavior. With coarse-head-only training, that oracle target matched the round_068 strict-point level and reduced latency to 6.27 ms. round_075 then combined the oracle teacher target with low-learning-rate reopening of stage3, lat2, lat3, and the coarse heads. It still held point_le_0_01_ratio at 0.7239, but reduced point_error_mean to 0.0094 and average inference to 6.24 ms, making it the current best saved split_v2 checkpoint under the user's metric order. The current conclusion is that the active best direction remains coarse-preserving, and the new oracle teacher target has reopened the search space: it does not yet raise the primary metric above 0.7239, but it improves the tie-breakers enough to replace round_068 with round_075 as the preferred split_v2 saved checkpoint. On 2026-03-26 a separate manual-only continuation family was run for the new datasets 202603-awe and 202603-guochenghao-yangzhou: round_076 learned the new data best at new holdout point_le_0_01_ratio 0.5000 but regressed the old split_v2 holdout to 0.6810; round_079 added scene and border-contact hard-case boosts but did not improve beyond that; round_080 added low-weight old-data replay and recovered the old split_v2 holdout to 0.6978, but new-data holdout fell back to 0.4125. round_081 to round_084 then verified coarse scene adaptation and explicit border-contact tagging, but still failed to break the 0.5000 new-data ceiling. round_085 to round_089 further verified a visibility-aware coarse-refine family: wiring, differentiable gating, manual process targets, and manual-only process masks were all corrected, but the process branch still stayed near-constant and never exceeded the 0.5000 new-data strict-point ceiling. round_090 then tested a state-aware candidate plus selector with an OpenCV-augmented pool, but the selector collapsed to the default base_final candidate and failed structurally. round_091 removed the selector and used the state-aware head directly as final output; that repaired the dead branch and matched round_076 at 0.5000 with lower latency 6.93 ms, making it the current best tie-break winner on the new-data holdout. round_092 then made the state-aware line strict-oriented and reopened stage3/lat2/lat3, which improved point_error_mean and max_corner geometry but regressed strict-point to 0.4625. round_093 then restricted the route to a binary OpenCV-vs-coarse selector and trained only candidate_selection_head; offline diagnostics showed the oracle still had 0.5625 strict-point headroom on holdout, but the saved model selected coarse on every holdout page and finished at 0.4750, which means the selector failed to overcome its initialization bias. round_094 kept the same binary candidate set and increased selector learning rate plus training length substantially. That made the selector move and improved validation to 0.5795, but holdout fell further to 0.4375 while selecting OpenCV on 4/20 holdout pages, proving the current validation target and route mechanism are misaligned. round_095 then returned to the coarse mainline and injected explicit hard-case sample_weight_multiplier values for near-border, suspected out-of-frame, low-contrast, and small-sample AWE pages. That improved geometry and wider-threshold metrics on the real holdout, but strict-point still stopped at 0.4750. round_096 then hot-started from round_095 epoch_001 and intentionally shortened training with softer augmentation. This recovered the new-data holdout strict-point back to 0.5000 and lowered latency further to 6.67 ms, making round_096 the current tie-break winner on the new-data holdout. round_097 then added random cutout-style occlusion augmentation on top of the weighted coarse line and fell back to 0.4500 at 7.32 ms. round_098 replaced that with edge-anchored occlusion targeted at border/out-of-frame cases; latency returned to 6.66 ms, but strict-point regressed again to 0.4375. round_099 then took the more targeted route: keep the round_096 coarse backbone frozen, enable a zero-init state_aware candidate head, and train only that head to correct border/out-of-frame corners. It regressed further to 0.3750 at 7.15 ms, which shows the residual edge-polish hypothesis is also not viable on the current supervision. During this work the checkpoint-selection rule for point_le_0_01_ratio was also corrected so that when strict-point ties, validation geometry outranks tiny latency noise. round_100 then introduced a true student-only hard mining replay: use round_096 itself to score the train set, rewrite sample_weight_multiplier from the student’s own strict misses and max-corner errors, and run a short replay on the same coarse mainline. That lifted the new-data holdout point_le_0_01_ratio from 0.5000 to 0.5250 at 6.96 ms. round_101 showed the next failure mode: accumulating those mined weights too aggressively pushes the train distribution too far, and holdout strict-point falls back to 0.4875. round_102 reset the weight baseline to round_096 while still mining from round_100 epoch_001. It preserved the 0.5250 strict-point level and improved several geometry tie-breakers, but latency rose to 7.17 ms, so round_100 remains the best new-data checkpoint under the user's strict-point-then-latency order. The current conclusion for the new-data continuation line is that self-hard-mining replay is the only validated direction that breaks the 0.5000 plateau, and its current local peak is 0.5250; within the tested neighborhood, round_100 is the preferred saved checkpoint. On 2026-03-26 a checkpoint snapshot bug was identified in the training loop: best_state used detach().cpu() without clone(), so CPU-trained student.pt artifacts could drift to the last epoch even when history selected an earlier best epoch. The code now snapshots cloned tensors, and the affected round_096/round_100 student.pt artifacts were corrected to their real epoch_001 weights. After re-running corrected continuations, round_103 targeted hard-mining and round_104 mild self-hard-mining both failed to exceed round_100 epoch_001=0.5250 on the new-data holdout, so the corrected manual-only new-data line should be treated as plateaued with round_100 remaining the preferred checkpoint. A further materially different curriculum line was then validated: round_105 trained a 100-page warmup subset consisting of all strict_hits<=1 train pages plus high-quality anchor pages, and round_106 consolidated that warmup back onto the full train set. This recovered the holdout only to 0.5000 at 6.69 ms and still failed to exceed round_100 epoch_001=0.5250, so the new-data line remains plateaued even under subset curriculum rather than global reweighting. After the corrected hard-mining and curriculum lines plateaued, the visibility-guided process-refine family was revalidated from the real round_100 epoch_001 checkpoint. round_107 enabled coarse_visibility_refine with manual-only process targets and trained only scene_context_head plus process_head; round_108 further reopened stage3, lat2, lat3, and the coarse heads together with process_head. Both rounds stalled at 0.4875 strict-point and slower latency, so the corrected process/gated refine line is now also considered exhausted on the new-data continuation benchmark. An offline oracle check then compared coarse/base_final/visibility_refined on the real round_100 epoch_001 checkpoint and found that per-corner mixing raises holdout point_le_0_01_ratio only from 0.5250 to 0.5375, which is too little headroom to justify a selector path. round_109 then tested a new coarse_strict local patch refine mode that reuses the existing strict_spatial_refine_head directly on top of coarse_quad with per-corner gates. That first structural probe fell back to 0.4875 strict-point at 9.09 ms, so the coarse-to-local strict patch refine family is now also considered exhausted. round_110 then tested whether better initialization alone could reopen the search space: an offline round_100 + round_102 checkpoint soup matched the 0.5250 strict-point level with better tie-breakers, but one epoch of polishing from that seed immediately dropped holdout strict-point back to 0.4875. round_111 then changed training dynamics rather than structure by adding optional EMA checkpoint evaluation; this recovered holdout strict-point to 0.5125, better than round_109/110, but still below round_100. round_112 then tested a new soft strict-hit supervision that directly optimized a sigmoidal <1% target, but holdout strict-point still fell to 0.4875. round_113 finally tested a zero-init coarse_residual_head on top of the corrected round_100 epoch_001 checkpoint; even that coarse-side residual exactness probe stayed at 0.4875, which confirms the manual-only new-data line is now plateaued not only for replay/process/selector families but also for the newly tested loss-shape and lightweight coarse-residual directions. The preferred manual-only new-data checkpoint remains round_100 epoch_001. round_114 then tested a non-border replay control on the old split_v1 by filtering train pages to hard_case_border_distance_min >= 0.02; holdout strict-point dropped further to 0.4375, so the old-split plateau is not explained by border-distribution skew alone. A new balanced-eval split was then created so 202603-awe is no longer excluded from holdout. round_115 combined that split with dataset-level boosting, but mixed holdout reached only 0.4643 and Yangzhou-only holdout regressed. round_116 repeated the same balanced-eval split without dataset boosting and recovered to mixed holdout point_le_0_01_ratio 0.4762 at 6.57 ms, with Yangzhou-only holdout at 0.4875 and the single-page AWE holdout still producing a usable prediction. The preferred manual-only new-data checkpoint on the old split remains round_100 epoch_001, while round_116 is the current reference checkpoint for the balanced-eval split. round_117 then migrated the old split_v1 self-hard-mining replay idea onto the balanced-eval split by reweighting train pages from round_116 epoch_001 errors and running a short replay. It only matched round_116 at 0.4762 strict-point and worsened latency to 7.15 ms, so the old hard-mining gain does not transfer cleanly to the newer split. round_118 then tested EMA-based trajectory smoothing on the same balanced-eval baseline. It also only matched 0.4762 and did not beat round_116 on latency. The current balanced-eval reference checkpoint therefore remains round_116, while round_100 epoch_001 still remains the preferred checkpoint on the older split_v1.
